provenance: Sol's v2.5.0 break-it review, §3 DESIGN — repair tokenization centrally rather than patching one consumer. The rule frozen here is his: compute the stem; if stemming CHANGED the token and produced fewer than three characters, reject the stem and keep the original surface token. A four-character derived floor would destroy families that work (dat, fix, sex, pay); an original-token floor would catch nothing, because really, stable, viable, national and rational all enter long; dropping the token outright would erase real concepts. Fallback is the only rule that separates the four cases.

degeneracy.question: Can stemming produce a fragment short enough to mean nothing, and does that fragment then get to act as a concept?
degeneracy.ruling: No transformed result may be shorter than three characters. A content word whose stem would be degenerate keeps its original surface form instead. `really` is additionally filtered as a stopword, in the company of `just`, `very`, `too` and `only`, so falling back to the surface cannot restore the co-fire defect v2.5.0 §1.4 found.

componentIsolation.question: Is `distinctiveBoost` the only thing a degenerate stem moves?
componentIsolation.ruling: No, and this pair is the proof. The two sentences differ by one intensifier. At freeze the `really` variant scores nearly double the `just` control, and it does so through four independent mechanisms at once: both coverage ratios, the distinctive boost, and the sparse-shared penalty it avoids by having a second shared token. A fix applied at one consumer would leave the other three.

cases.text: Marriage rates came up briefly at dinner, but the argument was just about which billing provider our startup should integrate.
cases.note: `just` is already a stopword, so this is what the sentence is worth once the intensifier stops being a concept.

expected.note: The two variants must score IDENTICALLY once `really` is filtered, because after filtering the two sentences tokenize to the same thing. The absolute value is deliberately not pinned here: it depends on the index-wide IDF, which this fix legitimately moves. What is pinned is the mechanism — the intensifier stops contributing anything, on every one of the four paths.

indexProvenance.question: Do degenerate stems get into the index itself, with real IDF weight behind them?
indexProvenance.ruling: They do, and the rule is stated over raw tokens rather than over the finished sets: for every word the canon contains, the representation the tokenizer accepts is either the word itself or at least three characters long. Stated that way it is origin-sensitive, which matters — `go`, `ai` and `us` are legitimate two-character ORIGINALS and must stay, while `going`, `users` and `using` collapsing onto them must not.

expected.note: Zero raw tokens whose accepted representation is both shortened and shorter than three characters, across every lexical surface of all 450 entries. The three token sets the matcher reads — _tokens, _distinctiveTokens, _surfaceTokens — inherit the property, because every one of them is built by the same tokenizer.

retrievalGuards.question: Does the fix remove the collisions without removing the concepts?
retrievalGuards.ruling: Both halves are asserted, because either one alone would be easy and wrong. The false collision must die; the five legitimate words must survive as themselves and keep matching the entries that use them. The guards assert TOKEN IDENTITY rather than a score, since the fix moves scores index-wide by design and a pinned number here would be a threshold assertion in disguise.
